Class CausalStreamsBuilder

java.lang.Object
io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley.CausalStreamsBuilder
public final class CausalStreamsBuilder extends Object
Builds a CausalTopology: exactly one causal stage — a set of source topics feeding a causal-decorated processor and forwarding to one or more sinks. Plays the same role StreamsBuilder plays for a plain Kafka Streams topology. 
CausalTopology topology = new CausalStreamsBuilder()
        .stream(List.of("orders", "payments"), Serdes.String(), eventSerde)
        .process(new EnrichmentProcessorSupplier())
        .to("orders.enriched", Serdes.String(), enrichedSerde)
        .build();

CausalStreams causalStreams = new CausalStreams(topology, props);
causalStreams.start();
Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(new Thread(causalStreams::close));

A causal topology is exactly one stream(...).process(...).to(...) chain. The fluent chain terminates in CausalProcessedStream.build(); there is no public build() on the builder and no way to open a second stage. Build a multi-stage pipeline as several applications chained topic to topic, which needs no coordination beyond the intermediate topic.

stream(Collection, Serde, Serde) fans several co-partitioned topics sharing one serde pair into one stage, CausalStream.merge(CausalStream) combines streams declared with different serdes, and CausalProcessedStream.to(String) declares each sink. Serdes may be omitted to defer to the runtime's default.key.serde / default.value.serde. Unlike the Kafka Streams DSL, sources and sinks take plain Serdes rather than Consumed/Produced, because the causal buffer needs the real serde to round-trip a held record across a restart.

Every source and sink a stage declares shares one StreamPartitioner (CausalProcessedStream.withPartitioner(StreamPartitioner), default the key-hash partitioner) so a shard never drifts onto different partitions across topics. The causal guarantee's preconditions still apply: co-partition related topics by key, keep processor effects closed over forward, and stamp every processor that sits between causally related topics.
